executive_preview: The week's strongest signal is a widening gap between automotive technology demonstrations and commercially deployable products. Tesla's Roadster reveal generated extensive coverage and demonstrated a prototype using SpaceX-derived cold-gas thrusters and underbody suction, but production timing, legality, pricing and repeatability remain unresolved. At the same time, Tesla's more commercially important autonomy strategy faces fresh regulatory scrutiny over school-zone behavior, while Volvo and Mercedes-Benz are expanding Nvidia partnerships to pursue more structured, safety-oriented automated driving systems.

lead_development.title: Chinese automakers are extending their competitive reach into Europe with increasingly broad product portfolios.
lead_development.what_happened: BYD presented large, fast-charging electric vehicles at the Paris Motor Show, Chery announced a 2027 U.K. launch for the iCaur V27, and AITO announced a European launch for four luxury SUVs in fall 2027.
lead_development.why_it_matters: European brands may face pressure not only in entry-level EVs but also in family SUVs and premium segments. Local tuning, distribution, regulatory compliance and brand trust will determine whether product capability converts into sustained market share.

signals.title: Tesla repositions the Roadster as a technology halo car, not a near-term volume product
signals.teaser: Tesla unveiled a redesigned next-generation Roadster at a SpaceX facility, showing a prototype driving on an inverted ramp, briefly lifting off, performing aerial maneuvers and recording a claimed 0-to-60-mph time of 0.81 seconds.

signals.title: Automakers are moving advanced driving systems toward Nvidia-centered software and compute platforms
signals.teaser: Volvo expanded its Nvidia partnership to use Hyperion, Halos and Alpamayo technologies for future supervised, hands-free and eventually more advanced automated-driving functions.

signals.title: Affordable EV positioning is becoming more tangible in the U.S. and China
signals.teaser: Ford opened invitations for its Fathom electric pickup, priced from $28,350 before destination, while GM's 2027 Bolt was tested as the least expensive U.S.

downside.title: Tesla's Roadster claims may create credibility and regulatory exposure if production specifications, legality or timing diverge from the demonstration.
downside.teaser: The vehicle has a history of delay, no final price was announced, thruster legality remains unclear and the company described the car as not necessarily safety optimized.

upside.title: Dealers can use transparent pricing, digital inspections and proactive outreach to defend service retention.
upside.teaser: Customers were reported to be using informal repair providers because they perceived dealership and repair-shop pricing as unclear or excessive.
